clue.text: Old country female comes down to entertain the Queen

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: an aircraft or a bird that comes down lands
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A woman descends on an old realm to host Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval county in the Low Countries, now split between Belgium, France and the Netherlands, was a historic country.

clue.text: Instrument's condition when given case of iron

indicators.note: a case encloses what it holds, so the iron letters wrap round the condition word

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A musical instrument's state once it is put in an iron casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched flute played in military bands is a musical instrument.

clue.text: A biblical city with a distinctive quality

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's birthplace in Genesis

explanation.surface: An ancient city from scripture has a special character about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atmosphere or air that seems to surround a person or place is a distinctive quality.

clue.text: Tragic suitors, sad, thrown into confusion

indicators.note: confusion is disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Rejected wooers, miserable and bewildered, in a sorry scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamitous outcome is catastrophic, which is close to tragic.

clue.text: Newspaper perused, we hear, by chief

indicators.note: we hear says the word for perused is heard, not seen, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: perused means read, in the past tense pronounced like the colour
top means chief, as in top dog

explanation.surface: A paper read by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, named for the red mastheads of papers like The Sun and the Mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid paper with a red masthead, a downmarket daily.

clue.text: Bitterness of everyone after end of squabbling

indicators.note: after places the everyone piece behind the letter from squabbling
the end of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of squabbling is taken

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone feels sour once a quarrel finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gall is bile, and by extension rancour or resentment: a synonym for bitterness of feeling.

clue.text: It's eaten? That's wrong — it's drunk

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner protests that a drink has been mistaken for food.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'It's' is ignored, leaving the letters ITSEATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured liqueur is a beverage, something one drinks.

clue.text: Boats less substantial beginning to sink to the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so the letter goes after the rest

parts.note: lighter means weighing less, less substantial

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Flimsier vessels start to sink and go down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighters are flat-bottomed barges that ferry goods between ships and the quay.

clue.text: If about to stay, you'll find a warm spot in winter

indicators.note: about signals that the two letters of if are turned around into a new order

parts.note: to reside somewhere is to stay or live there

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay on promises somewhere cosy when it is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal on just the two letters before it, a reversal in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The area beside a hearth is where people gather to keep warm in the cold months.

clue.text: Heather uses loveless language

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O, so loveless means without an O

parts.note: lingo is slang for a language or jargon

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather speaks in a cold, unloving tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant. 'loveless' drops O (love = nil) from LINGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ling is the common heather, Calluna vulgaris, the purple-flowered moorland shrub.

clue.text: Keeping under surveillance a top man determined to get outside

indicators.note: the word for determined goes outside the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: stout means resolute, determined, as in stout resistance
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: A resolute boss is under watch as he tries to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching a place covertly over time, as police do, is a stakeout.

clue.text: Matters son mismanaged — lots of different things

indicators.note: something mismanaged is handled badly and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A son has made a mess of the family's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mismanaged' rearranges the ten letters of MATTERS SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed collection of varied items, like a box of chocolates of several kinds.

clue.text: Measures teachers changed

indicators.note: changed means altered in arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Staff at a school bring in new policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measures' looks like a verb or policies; it is units of area.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land area, ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Not working, finished being hurt

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for an adjective meaning hurt in feelings

parts.note: a machine switched off is not working
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Someone off sick and done for is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slighted or affronted is to have one's feelings wounded.

clue.text: You will need some beef for this!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a task will take some muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in bEEF FOR This; 'beef' also means muscle power, so the whole clue hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard work or exertion is what any demanding task requires, so it is what you will need.

clue.text: Heartless sir grabbing woman — one may be on thin ice!

definitions.text: one may be on thin ice!

indicators.note: grabbing means holding something in its grip, so the woman goes inside
heartless removes the central letter of sir, leaving its two outer letters

parts.note: Kate is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A gentleman, short of feeling, seizes a woman: a risky move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter of sir; 'grabbing' has what remains take the woman inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person gliding on blades over a frozen pond risks thin ice, literally as well as figuratively.

clue.text: Stagnant swamp in Berkshire town

definitions.meaning: a bog or marsh of standing water
a large town west of London near Windsor, in the English county of Berkshire

explanation.surface: A stagnant marsh is found in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is a county west of London; the town is famously mocked in John Betjeman's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a muddy bog and a Berkshire town, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: To English, Scottish game very embarrassing

parts.note: curling, sliding stones over ice, is a game of Scottish origin

explanation.surface: Explaining a Scottish sport to an Englishman proves awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling slides granite stones along ice towards a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so awkward it makes the toes clench in the shoes is cringe-making.

clue.text: Three performers from choir turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, across the word break

explanation.surface: Three singers from the choir arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like one phrase meaning arrived, but 'turned' supplies the hidden T and only 'up' reverses: choIR Turned gives OIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three musicians or singers is a trio.

clue.text: Name of man ending in some Asian countries

definitions.meaning: a male first name, short for Stanley
the suffix meaning land, as in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A man's name ends several Asian country names.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Stanley is also the Persian suffix closing Pakistan or Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Impolite and cross, by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word for cross is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: Someone seems rude and angry, judging by their tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a second definition meaning angry; it is ROOD, a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-mannered and discourteous behaviour is impolite.

clue.text: Despot in car, an unreliable one, mostly

parts.note: auto is a short form of automobile, a car

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for a rickety car

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, unreliable car

explanation.surface: A tyrant rides about in a clapped-out vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to car, so the unreliable one is another car: CRATE, cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with absolute, unchecked power is a tyrant or despot.

clue.text: District I had found in home counties

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England, SE
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an area they once discovered near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties bordering London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A part of a town, as in the West Side or the north side, is a district.

clue.text: Nuts who'd contrived closure of business?

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was it lunatics who engineered the firm's collapse?
explanation.definitionFit: When a factory or company ceases operating it closes, a cessation of trading.
